findings.title: A blocking blind review is posted as qodo-gate 'NOT DONE: N with a label the gate can't read, 0 High or Medium'
findings.why: When the blind review reproduces findings, the runner posts gate(n, s, prHead, { state: 'fix', blocking: b.blocking, lows: [] }). gateStatus/blockingWhy classify blocking entries by Qodo's attribution_status and action_level, which blind findings don't have (they carry `severity`), so every reproduced High/Medium is counted as 'with a label the gate can't read' and the public status on the PR head says that, not that the blind review reproduced High or Medium findings. The owner is told to look for an unreadable Qodo label that doesn't exist. Fix: give the blind failure its own description, or map blind findings into the gate's shape before posting.

findings.title: The blind reviewer can still learn Qodo's findings from commit messages, test names and code comments
findings.why: BLIND bans reading .agent/review.md and similar files, but allows git log/git show and reading the tree. On this branch the head commit is 'fix: Qodo's findings on #107: exit codes, write scope, blind status, proofs, local rounds', tests are named '#107 03259bcb: …' and comments say '(Qodo on #107)', so the reviewer sees what Qodo flagged. `node --test` on a test file it writes also runs arbitrary code that can read the banned .agent/ files, so the read bans don't hold. The PR's claim that the reviewer 'can't read Qodo's review' is only partly enforced. I couldn't write a unit repro for this: it's about the agent's permission profile, not a pure function.

findings.title: A ticket that makes no claims about existing code always stops at the Wisdom check
findings.why: wisdomVerdict returns 'invalid' for { claims: [] }, and wisdomCheck throws Stop on 'invalid'. A ticket that is purely new work, with nothing to say about main, can never get past gate 1, even when the investigator worked correctly and found nothing to check. This may be on purpose (the tests assert it), but it means an honest empty result counts the same as a broken run.

findings.title: mayPostSuccess reads only the first 100 statuses of the head
findings.why: statusesOf fetches commits/<sha>/statuses?per_page=100 once (Rule 7 says to read every page). If more than 100 newer statuses sit on a head, the blind-review status drops off the page, mayPostSuccess sees none and allows a manual --post success even though the blind review failed. That's unlikely, since the runner posts only on change.

findings.title: A real repro whose output mentions 'SyntaxError' never blocks
findings.why: red() rejects any run whose output contains SyntaxError anywhere, including an assertion message or a test name (for example a bug in a parser that should throw SyntaxError). A real assertion failure would then be filed as 'not reproduced'.
